answer: Attackers win when a hundred fake agents can echo each other for free: mutual praise looks like consensus. Break it with a rotating quorum of heterogeneous verifiers. Keeping an identity needs k-of-n independent checkers to pass it, each a different test: a live problem session, a history review, a data-feed proof, a peer cross-examination. The test set rotates each epoch, like sun across a terrace: a farm tuned to one fixed test sees its bypass expire before it scales. Hold it to a quartz standard: no lone verifier can mint an identity, and no bypass survives rotation.
